subject.title: Device identity generation should not depend on browser Secure Context — breaks HTTP reverse-proxy deployments

question: Should OpenClaw allow persistent Control UI browser device identity to be generated and used from non-localhost plain HTTP origins?
rationale: The remaining change is not just a hash implementation swap; it decides whether a remote plaintext browser context may hold and present operator device identity after receiving UI code over an unauthenticated transport.

options.title: Keep secure-context default
options.body: Continue rejecting remote plain-HTTP browser device identity by default and focus on warnings, HTTPS/Tailscale guidance, and existing break-glass paths.

options.title: Add explicit plaintext opt-in
options.body: Permit remote HTTP browser identity only behind a clearly named operator-selected policy with docs, audit warnings, and upgrade tests.

options.title: Remove the gate globally
options.body: Always attempt browser identity generation without `crypto.subtle`, accepting the broader plaintext transport trust change as the default behavior.

recommendation.title: Keep secure-context default
recommendation.body: Continue rejecting remote plain-HTTP browser device identity by default and focus on warnings, HTTPS/Tailscale guidance, and existing break-glass paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The central device-identity and secure Control UI auth policy commits trace to this owner path, and this decision affects that boundary directly.
